jurisdiction.name: Bangladesh
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Bangladesh has no AI-specific law and no adopted AI policy: the ICT Division's National AI Policy 2026-2030 was still a draft (version 1.1, January 2026). AI is addressed through clauses in 2026 Acts of parliament that replaced 2025 ordinances: the Cyber Security Act covers offences involving AI agents and AI tools, the National Data Management Act allows AI applications on the government data exchange, and an amendment to the election law makes AI-generated election disinformation a corrupt practice. The 2026 Personal Data Protection Act created a data protection authority but has no AI-specific provisions.
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The draft National AI Policy is recorded as a draft, and the 2020 AI strategy and the 2024 draft policy could not be found on reachable official sites and are listed as leads.

instruments.issuing_authority: Information and Communication Technology Division, Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology
instruments.summary: Draft national AI policy for 2026-2030 published by the ICT Division as a notice. It sets Bangladesh AI principles (including human oversight and accountability), a foundation of regulatory, data-governance, infrastructure, procurement, digital-media/deepfake, rights, civil-service capacity and risk-management measures (including a risk-based approach and algorithmic impact assessments), and priority sectors from public services and education to health, agriculture and national security. Implementation would rest on an Independent Oversight Committee, an AI Innovation Fund and a Project Implementation Office, with a 2028 mid-term review, a sunset provision and a legislative pathway towards AI legislation.
instruments.current_status: Draft V1.1 published on the ICT Division notice board on 14 January 2026 (notice archive date 30 June 2026) with the PDF as its download. Not adopted as of 12 October 2026: no final policy found on the ICT Division site. It follows an earlier draft National AI Policy 2024 and the 2020 National Strategy for AI (both held as leads). The draft refers to the Personal Data Protection Ordinance 2025, the National Data Governance Ordinance 2025 and the 'Cyber Safety Ordinance' 2025 as the existing legal base.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main forward-looking national AI policy document; would set the national AI governance structure.

instruments.issuing_authority: President of Bangladesh (ordinance under Article 93(1) of the Constitution)
instruments.summary: Interim-government ordinance that repealed the Cyber Security Act 2023, set up the National Cyber Security Agency and Council, and defined cyber offences. It wrote AI into the law: definitions cover AI software agents, large language models and AI tools, and offences such as unlawful access to critical information infrastructure apply expressly to users of AI tools and to AI agents.
instruments.current_status: Promulgated 21 May 2025 with immediate effect; amended by the Cyber Security (Amendment) Ordinance 2025; repealed and re-enacted by the Cyber Security Act 2026 (Act No. 81 of 2026), as the portal notes.

instruments.summary: Act re-enacting the Cyber Security Ordinance 2025: it establishes the National Cyber Security Agency, Council, CERTs and digital forensic labs and defines cyber offences and penalties. Its definitions expressly include AI software agents, large language models and AI tools, and offences apply to software developers and users of AI tools (e.g. section 17 on unlawful access to critical information infrastructure, up to 5 years' imprisonment or BDT 5 million fine) and to forgery by an AI agent.
instruments.current_status: In force; enacted 10 April 2026 and deemed effective from 21 May 2025 (section 1(2)). Amended by the Cyber Security (Amendment) Act 2026 (Act No. 99 of 2026, 1 July 2026), which contains no AI-specific text.

instruments.english_title: Personal Data Protection Ordinance, 2025 (Ordinance No. 61 of 2025)
instruments.issuing_authority: President of Bangladesh (ordinance under Article 93(1) of the Constitution)
instruments.summary: Bangladesh's first comprehensive personal data protection ordinance, treating personal data as owned by the data subject and requiring lawful, consent-based processing with data-subject rights, controller and processor duties and an authority. It governs personal data used to train and run AI systems but contains no AI-specific provisions.
instruments.current_status: Promulgated 6 November 2025; amended by the Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Ordinance 2026; repealed by the Personal Data Protection Act 2026 (Act No. 63 of 2026), as the portal notes.

instruments.english_title: Personal Data Protection Act, 2026 (Act No. 63 of 2026)
instruments.summary: Comprehensive data protection law replacing the 2025 ordinance: it applies extraterritorially, sets lawful bases and conditions for processing (including sensitive data and children's data), data-subject rights, security and retention duties for controllers and processors, and a regulator that can set technical standards. It governs personal data used in AI training and deployment; it has no AI-specific or automated-decision provisions.
instruments.current_status: In force; enacted 10 April 2026 and deemed effective from 6 November 2025, except section 23 and sections 31-35, which commence on a date the government notifies in the gazette after 18 months (section 1(3)).

instruments.english_title: National Data Management Ordinance, 2025 (Ordinance No. 60 of 2025)
instruments.issuing_authority: President of Bangladesh (ordinance under Article 93(1) of the Constitution)
instruments.summary: Ordinance creating a national data management and interoperability authority and the National Responsible Data Exchange (NRDEX) for government data sharing. It expressly allowed AI applications on NRDEX to simplify administration and service delivery and to fight corruption, limited to listed purposes, and put an AI/large-language-model expert on the authority's board.
instruments.current_status: Promulgated 6 November 2025; repealed by the National Data Management Act 2026 (Act No. 80 of 2026), as the portal notes. The draft National AI Policy refers to it as the 'National Data Governance Ordinance'.

instruments.english_title: National Data Management Act, 2026 (Act No. 80 of 2026)
instruments.summary: Act governing national management, sharing and interoperability of government data through a national data management authority and the NRDEX exchange. Section 30(7) permits AI applications on NRDEX for administrative improvement, project appraisal, public procurement review, tax/customs/VAT evasion detection, statistical audits and citizen services, and the authority's board includes an AI/large-language-model expert.
instruments.current_status: In force; enacted 10 April 2026 and deemed effective from 6 November 2025 (section 1(2)).

instruments.english_title: Representation of the People (Amendment) Ordinance, 2025 (Ordinance No. 56 of 2025)
instruments.issuing_authority: President of Bangladesh (ordinance under Article 93(1) of the Constitution)
instruments.summary: Ordinance amending the Representation of the People Order 1972 ahead of the 2026 parliamentary election. Its new Article 73A made it a corrupt practice to knowingly create or spread false or misleading content, whether made manually or generated by AI tools, to harm a candidate or influence the result, or to use automated bots, fake accounts or synthetic media to spread false information during the election period.
instruments.current_status: Promulgated 3 November 2025 with immediate effect; repealed by the Representation of the People (Amendment) Act 2026 (Act No. 3 of 2026), as the portal notes.

instruments.english_title: Representation of the People (Amendment) Act, 2026 (Act No. 3 of 2026)
instruments.summary: Act re-enacting the 2025 amendments to the Representation of the People Order 1972. Its Article 73A makes it a corrupt practice, between the election notification and the gazetting of results, to knowingly create, publish or share false or misleading content, including AI-generated content, to harm a candidate or influence the result, or to use bots, fake accounts or synthetic media to spread false information about candidates, parties or the Election Commission.
instruments.current_status: In force; enacted 10 April 2026 and deemed effective from 3 November 2025 (section 1(2)). The Act is published in English with a Bengali enacting text.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. aipolicy.gov.bd expired TLS certificate/503; bcc.portal.gov.bd TLS host mismatch/503; ecs.gov.bd gazette section and dpp.gov.bd gazette search not reached (consolidated texts on bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd used, 2025 ordinance and 2026 Act volumes grepped for AI terms). Ordinances recorded as binding_law (Art. 93(1)) and superseded by the 2026 Acts. Not a party to Convention 108. Units covered: Law: Laws of Bangladesh portal (bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd): 2025 ordinance and 2026 Act volumes scanned; full texts read for the Cyber Security Ordinance 2025/Act 2026, Personal Data Protection Ordinance 2025/Act 2026, National Data Management Ordinance 2025/Act 2026 and Representation of the People (Amendment) Ordinance 2025/Act 2026. No AI-specific Act and no AI bill found. Cyber Security (Amendment) Act 2026 checked: no AI text.; Government: ICT Division site: policies, laws, guidelines and strategy papers, notices; draft National AI Policy 2026-2030 V1.1 read in full. The 2020 AI strategy and 2024 draft AI policy were not found on any reachable official site (leads). a2i: no AI guideline document found via search.; Ministries: Searched, nothing found: no ministry-level AI strategy, guideline or playbook (education, health, law, finance) found on official sites; the National Data Management Act 2026 s.30(7) is the only public-sector AI rule found.; Regulators: Bangladesh Bank: no published AI circular or guideline (drafting reported; lead). BTRC, Bangladesh Computer Council/National Cyber Security Agency, data protection authority (newly created under the 2026 Act), competition commission: searched, no AI-specific documents found. Election Commission AI code-of-conduct rule held as lead.. Not reached: aipolicy.gov.bd (expired TLS certificate; WebFetch 503); bcc.portal.gov.bd legacy portal (TLS host mismatch; WebFetch 503); ecs.gov.bd gazette section (not searched directly); dpp.gov.bd / bgpress gazette search (not used; bdlaws consolidated texts used instead). Could not verify: National Strategy for AI 2020 (no reachable official copy); Draft National AI Policy 2024 (aipolicy.gov.bd unreachable); BCC Draft Version 3.0 National Strategy for AI (bcc.portal.gov.bd unreachable); Bangladesh Bank AI policy/office order (not published); Election Commission code of conduct AI rule (gazette not read). transparency, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, sectoral, international: no material found.
